name: IA-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+15 district gives Republicans a structural edge in the open seat
McGowan's large fundraising and outside-support advantage over Dawson
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only a few percent
No public polling; a historic Democratic wave would be needed to compete
model.rationale: The open seat sits in one of the most Republican districts in the nation, and the Republican nominee's large fundraising edge and lopsided market pricing leave the Democrat needing a historic swing to compete.
model.watch: A severe national backlash against Republicans or an unexpected Republican stumble could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require a historically large shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Randy Feenstra (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Iowa's fourth district is among the most Republican seats in the country, and Randy Feenstra's retirement to run for governor does not change that underlying lean. Chris McGowan enters the general election as the clear favorite, with Polymarket pricing a Democratic win at only a few percent. No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, candidate fundraising, and market pricing.

McGowan has raised roughly $850,000 and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat David Dawson, who has raised about $240,000 with modest cash on hand. Outside groups have spent in support of McGowan while the Democratic side has drawn little outside help. A favorable national environment for Democrats would need to be historically large to put this seat in play; the race is rated Likely Republican.
